desc: Brute-force BFS for tiny N, X, Y to guess the exact reachability criterion (test popcount + boundary positions mod g, X=Y case, boundary creation/destruction).
Run the full n≤9 sweep with instrumented analyze(); determine whether invariant_tuple separates components and whether greedy canonical form is bijective; identify all failure cases.

Derive exact run-length transfer rules for Op A (at 0|1 boundary) and Op B (at 1|0 boundary), including run shrink-to-zero merging, end-absorption thresholds, and X=Y behavior; formulate refined invariant (popcount + interior boundary positions mod slide_unit + capped first/last run lengths).

Run the full n≤9 sweep and collect all cases where test (2b) fails; classify failures into "tuple too coarse" (frozen-end cases like n=4,X=1,Y=2 `1000` vs `0100`) vs "tuple too fine" (end-absorption changing the boundary list).

Fix the invariant based on failure classification: if boundary list is too fine under absorption, record only interior boundary positions mod g plus count of absorbable boundaries at each end; if too coarse, strengthen end-run encoding; re-test until (2b) separates perfectly on n≤9.
Prove sufficiency: greedy left-to-right boundary sliding transforms S into T whenever invariants hold, respecting run-length prerequisites (≥X zeros / ≥Y ones adjacent).
Handle edge cases: X=Y, X+Y>N (check S==T), all-equal strings, single boundary, N small.
Implement O(N) Python solution: parse input, run-encode S and T, check invariants + greedy reachability, print Yes/No.
Validate on provided samples and stress-test against brute-force BFS for small N.
